text: What base does the binary number system use?
optionA: Base 2
optionB: Base 8
optionC: Base 10
optionD: Base 16
explanation: Binary is base 2; each digit (bit) can only be 0 or 1.

text: Convert the denary number 25 to binary.

Convert the denary number 178 to hexadecimal.
optionA: B2
optionB: A8
optionC: C2
optionD: B4
explanation: 178 ÷ 16 = 11 remainder 2; 11 in hex = B; so 178 = B2.

text: What is the denary value of hexadecimal 3F?
Convert the hexadecimal value A9 to binary.
explanation: A = 1010 in binary; 9 = 1001 in binary; together = 10101001.

text: Why is hexadecimal often used to represent binary data?
optionA: It is base 16 so it is easier for computers to process
optionB: It is a shorter and more human-readable form of binary
optionC: It can represent negative numbers that binary cannot
optionD: It uses fewer transistors in hardware
explanation: One hex digit represents exactly four bits; this makes long binary strings much shorter and easier to read.

text: How many different values can be represented by one hexadecimal digit?
explanation: Hexadecimal uses digits 0–9 and letters A–F; that is 16 different values per digit.

text: What is the maximum positive denary value that can be stored in an 8-bit register (unsigned)?
explanation: An 8-bit register holds 2^8 = 256 values; from 0 to 255.

text: Convert the binary number 0111 1111 to hexadecimal.
optionB: 7E
optionC: 7F
optionD: 8F

text: In which area of computer science is hexadecimal commonly used to represent data?
optionA: Music files only
optionB: Memory addresses and colour codes
optionC: Spreadsheet formulas
optionD: Printer output
explanation: Hex is widely used for memory addresses; MAC addresses; RGB colour codes; and machine code.

text: What is the denary value of 0xFF?
Convert denary 100 to binary.
Convert hexadecimal C0 to denary.
How many bits are needed to represent one hexadecimal digit?
explanation: Each hex digit maps to exactly 4 bits (a nibble).

text: Add the two 8-bit binary numbers 0011 1010 and 0100 0110. What is the result?
What happens when the result of adding two 8-bit binary numbers exceeds the maximum 8-bit value?
optionA: The result is stored using 16 bits automatically
optionB: An overflow error occurs and some data is lost
optionC: The CPU rounds down to the nearest value
optionD: The numbers are converted to hexadecimal first
explanation: An overflow error occurs when the result is too large to fit in the register; the most significant bit is lost.

text: A logical left shift of 1 position is applied to 0001 0100. What is the result?
explanation: Shifting left by 1 moves every bit one place to the left and adds a 0 on the right: 00101000.

text: A logical right shift of 2 positions is applied to 1110 0000. What is the result?
explanation: Shifting right by 2 moves every bit two places right; zeros fill from the left: 00111000.

text: What effect does a logical left shift by 1 position have on a positive unsigned binary integer?
optionA: It divides the value by 2
optionB: It multiplies the value by 2
optionC: It increases the value by 1
optionD: It has no effect on the value
explanation: A left shift by 1 is equivalent to multiplying by 2 (as long as no bits overflow).

text: A logical right shift by 1 position is applied to 0001 1000. What is the result?
explanation: 0001 1000 shifted right by 1 gives 0000 1100; a zero is added at the most significant bit.

text: What happens to bits that are shifted out of the end of an 8-bit register during a logical shift?
optionA: They wrap around to the other end
optionB: They are lost
optionC: They are stored in the carry flag only
optionD: They are added to the original value
explanation: In a logical shift; bits shifted beyond the register boundary are discarded.

text: A logical left shift of 3 positions is applied to 0000 0001. What is the denary value of the result?
Add 0101 1001 and 0011 0100. What is the result?
What is the purpose of an overflow flag in a CPU?
optionA: To count how many additions have been performed
optionB: To signal that an arithmetic result is too large for the register
optionC: To indicate the CPU has run out of memory
optionD: To show when two equal values are added
explanation: The overflow flag is set when an arithmetic result cannot fit in the destination register; indicating data loss.

text: How many times larger is the value after a logical left shift of 2 positions compared to the original (assuming no overflow)?
explanation: A left shift by 2 multiplies by 2^2 = 4.

text: A right shift by 3 is applied to 0100 0000 (64 in denary). What is the result in denary?
What is the 8-bit two's complement representation of the denary number +19?
explanation: Positive numbers in two's complement are the same as normal binary: 19 = 00010011.

text: What is the 8-bit two's complement representation of the denary number −5?
What is the range of denary values that can be represented using 8-bit two's complement?
explanation: 8-bit two's complement represents −128 (10000000) to +127 (01111111).

text: What is the first step in finding the two's complement of a binary number?
optionA: Add 1 to the original number
optionB: Invert all the bits
optionC: Remove the most significant bit
optionD: Double the original value
explanation: The two's complement method: first invert all bits (one's complement); then add 1.

text: What does the most significant bit (MSB) indicate in a two's complement number?
optionA: The parity of the number
optionB: Whether the number is positive (0) or negative (1)
optionC: The magnitude of the number
optionD: The number base being used
explanation: In two's complement; a 0 MSB means positive and a 1 MSB means negative.

text: What is the denary value of the 8-bit two's complement number 1111 0111?
explanation: 1111 0111 has MSB=1 so it is negative. Invert: 0000 1000; add 1: 0000 1001 = 9; so the value is −9.

text: Convert +127 to 8-bit two's complement.
explanation: 127 in binary is 01111111; positive numbers use the same representation as unsigned binary.

text: Convert −1 to 8-bit two's complement.
Convert −128 to 8-bit two's complement.
explanation: −128 is the minimum 8-bit two's complement value; represented as 10000000.

text: What is the main advantage of two's complement over sign-and-magnitude for negative numbers?
optionA: It allows larger positive values
optionB: Arithmetic operations work the same way for positive and negative numbers
optionC: It uses fewer bits to store a number
optionD: It is easier for humans to read
explanation: With two's complement; the same addition circuit works for both positive and negative numbers; there is also no negative zero.

text: What is the denary value of the two's complement number 0001 1010?
Convert −20 to 8-bit two's complement.
What does ASCII stand for?
optionA: Automated System Code for Information Interchange
optionB: American Standard Code for Information Interchange
optionC: Advanced Standard Code for Integrated Input
optionD: Automated Standard Code for Interchange and Input
explanation: ASCII = American Standard Code for Information Interchange; a character encoding standard.

text: Why does a computer need to convert text characters to binary?
optionA: Because computers can only process binary data
optionB: Because text characters are too complex to store directly
optionC: Because binary is more compact than text
optionD: Because it makes text easier for humans to read
explanation: All data processed by a computer must be converted to binary first.

text: How many bits does standard ASCII use to represent each character?
explanation: Standard ASCII uses 7 bits; giving 128 possible characters. Extended ASCII uses 8 bits.

text: Why was Unicode developed?
optionA: To replace binary representation
optionB: To allow a greater range of characters including different languages and emojis
optionC: To make file sizes smaller
optionD: To speed up text processing
explanation: ASCII only covers basic Latin characters; Unicode supports thousands of characters from many languages; symbols and emojis.

text: Which of the following is a key difference between ASCII and Unicode?
optionA: ASCII can only represent numbers; Unicode can represent letters
optionB: Unicode allows more bits per character and covers a greater range
optionC: ASCII uses 16 bits; Unicode uses 7 bits
optionD: Unicode is only used in email while ASCII is used everywhere else
explanation: Unicode requires more bits per character but supports far more characters than ASCII.

text: A file contains 500 characters stored using 8-bit ASCII. What is the file size in bits?
explanation: 500 characters × 8 bits each = 4000 bits.

text: If a text file uses Unicode with 16 bits per character and contains 200 characters; what is the file size in bytes?
explanation: 200 characters × 16 bits = 3200 bits = 400 bytes.

text: What is a character set?
optionA: A set of physical keys on a keyboard
optionB: A defined collection of characters with assigned binary codes
optionC: A database of all possible text documents
optionD: A set of fonts available to a computer
explanation: A character set maps characters (letters; digits; symbols) to unique binary values.

text: What disadvantage does Unicode have compared to ASCII for simple English text documents?
optionA: Unicode cannot represent the letter A
optionB: Unicode requires more storage space per character
optionC: Unicode is not supported by modern systems
optionD: Unicode cannot be used in email
explanation: Unicode uses more bits per character than ASCII; so storing the same English text requires more space.

text: Why does text need to be converted to binary to be processed by a computer?
optionA: Binary is the only signal level a CPU's transistors use
optionB: Text is processed faster as binary
optionC: Binary can store more information per character
optionD: Text files are too large without binary conversion
explanation: Computers use binary (0s and 1s) at hardware level because transistors have two states.

text: What is sampling in the context of digital sound?
optionA: Playing back a recorded sound
optionB: Measuring the amplitude of a sound wave at regular intervals
optionC: Transmitting audio over a network
optionD: Filtering out background noise
explanation: Analogue sound is sampled by measuring the amplitude at regular time intervals; creating discrete values that can be stored as binary.

text: What is the sample rate of a digital audio recording?
optionA: The number of bits used per sample
optionB: The number of samples taken per second
optionC: The file size of the audio recording
optionD: The quality rating of the microphone
explanation: Sample rate is measured in hertz (Hz) and means how many amplitude measurements are taken each second.

text: What is the sample resolution (bit depth) of a digital audio recording?
optionA: The number of samples taken per second
optionB: The file size per second of audio
optionC: The number of bits used to represent each sample
optionD: The number of channels in the recording
explanation: Sample resolution (also called bit depth) determines how many different amplitude levels can be recorded.

text: If a sound is recorded with a higher sample rate; what happens to the quality and file size?
optionA: Quality decreases; file size decreases
optionB: Quality increases; file size increases
optionC: Quality increases; file size decreases
optionD: Quality decreases; file size increases
explanation: More samples per second means the waveform is reproduced more accurately (better quality) but more data is stored (larger file).

text: If a sound is recorded with a higher sample resolution; what happens?
optionA: Both quality and file size increase
optionB: Quality increases but file size decreases
optionC: File size increases but quality decreases
optionD: Neither quality nor file size is affected
explanation: More bits per sample means more amplitude levels (better accuracy); but each sample takes more space.

text: A sound is recorded at 44 100 Hz sample rate; 16-bit resolution; for 10 seconds. What is the file size in bits?
explanation: 44 100 samples/s × 16 bits × 10 s = 7 056 000 bits.

text: A recording is made at 8 kHz sample rate and 8-bit resolution. If a recording at 44.1 kHz with 16-bit resolution is made instead; by approximately how much does the file size increase?
optionA: About 11 times larger
optionB: About 2 times larger
optionC: About 44 times larger
optionD: About 22 times larger
explanation: 44100/8000 ≈ 5.5; 16/8 = 2; combined ≈ 11 times larger.

text: Why does a higher sample rate produce better quality audio?
optionA: It uses more bits per sample
optionB: It captures more of the sound wave's detail per second
optionC: It reduces background noise
optionD: It allows the file to be compressed more
explanation: More samples per second results in a more accurate digital representation of the original analogue sound wave.

text: What does a 16-bit sample resolution tell you?
optionA: Each second of audio uses 16 samples
optionB: Each sample can have one of 2^16 = 65 536 different amplitude levels
optionC: The recording is made at 16 000 Hz
optionD: The audio file contains 16 channels
explanation: 16-bit resolution means each sample stores 16 bits; representing 65 536 possible amplitude levels.

text: A 1-minute stereo sound file is recorded at 22 050 Hz; 16-bit resolution. How many bits are in the file? (Stereo = 2 channels)
What is a pixel?
optionA: The file format used to store images
optionB: The smallest individual element in a digital image
optionC: A unit of colour depth
optionD: The name for the entire image grid
explanation: Pixel stands for picture element; it is the smallest addressable unit in a digital raster image.

text: What is the resolution of a digital image?
optionA: The number of colours it can display
optionB: The number of pixels in the image
optionC: The file size in megabytes
optionD: The brightness level of the image
explanation: Resolution refers to the total number of pixels (e.g. 1920×1080); a higher resolution means more detail.

text: What is colour depth?
optionA: The number of pixels in an image
optionB: The number of bits used to represent the colour of each pixel
optionC: The physical size of the image on screen
optionD: The brightness contrast between pixels
explanation: Colour depth (bit depth) determines how many different colours each pixel can represent; e.g. 24-bit = 16.7 million colours.

text: A 24-bit colour image has a resolution of 100 × 80 pixels. What is the file size in bits?
If the resolution of an image is increased while colour depth stays the same; what happens?
optionA: Quality decreases and file size decreases
optionB: Quality increases and file size increases
optionC: Quality increases but file size stays the same
optionD: File size increases but quality stays the same
explanation: More pixels = more detail (higher quality) and more data to store (larger file).

text: If colour depth increases from 8-bit to 24-bit; what happens to the number of possible colours per pixel?
optionA: Triples from 256 to 768
optionB: Increases from 256 to 16 777 216
optionC: Doubles from 256 to 512
optionD: Remains the same at 256
explanation: 8-bit = 2^8 = 256 colours; 24-bit = 2^24 = 16 777 216 colours.

text: A 1-bit colour depth image can only display two colours. Which are those two colours in a typical black and white image?
optionA: Red and blue
optionB: Black and white
optionC: Green and yellow
optionD: Grey and white
explanation: 1 bit per pixel = 2^1 = 2 possible values; typically black (0) and white (1).

text: An image has a resolution of 200 × 150 pixels and uses 8-bit colour. What is the file size in bytes?
Why does increasing colour depth increase file size?
optionA: Each pixel needs more bits to store its colour information
optionB: More pixels are added to the image
optionC: The image dimensions increase
optionD: The file format becomes more complex
explanation: Greater colour depth requires more bits per pixel; so the same number of pixels takes up more storage.

text: Which change would most significantly reduce the file size of a bitmap image?
optionA: Renaming the file
optionB: Reducing the colour depth from 24-bit to 8-bit
optionC: Changing the file extension from .bmp to .jpg
optionD: Rotating the image 90 degrees
explanation: Reducing colour depth reduces bits per pixel; directly reducing file size (a file extension change alone changes nothing without encoding changes).

text: What is the main purpose of data compression?
optionA: To encrypt data for security
optionB: To reduce the file size of data
optionC: To speed up CPU processing
optionD: To convert analogue data to digital
explanation: Compression reduces the number of bits needed to represent data; saving storage space and reducing transmission time.

text: What is the difference between lossless and lossy compression?
optionA: Lossless removes duplicate data permanently; lossy stores all original data
optionB: Lossless allows perfect reconstruction of the original; lossy permanently removes some data
optionC: Lossless is faster; lossy produces larger files
optionD: Lossless only works for images; lossy only works for audio
explanation: Lossless compression preserves all original data; lossy discards some data to achieve greater compression.

text: Which of these would be best stored using lossless compression?
optionA: A music file for casual listening
optionB: A photograph shared on social media
optionC: A medical X-ray image that must retain all detail
optionD: A movie file for streaming
explanation: Medical images must not lose any diagnostic detail; so lossless compression is essential.

text: Which of the following is an example of a lossy compression format?
optionA: PNG
optionB: BMP
optionC: WAV
optionD: MP3
explanation: MP3 uses lossy compression; discarding audio frequencies less perceptible to human hearing.

text: Which of the following is an example of a lossless compression format?
optionA: JPEG
optionB: MP3
optionC: PNG
optionD: MPEG
explanation: PNG uses lossless compression; the original pixel data can be reconstructed exactly.

text: How does run-length encoding (RLE) compress data?
optionA: By removing every other bit
optionB: By replacing repeated consecutive identical values with a count and that value
optionC: By encrypting common sequences of bits
optionD: By converting data to a shorter number base
explanation: RLE finds runs of repeated values and stores them as (count; value); e.g. AAAABBB → 4A3B.

text: A row of pixels is: WWWWWWBBBBW. Using RLE; how would this be encoded?
optionA: W6B4W1
optionB: 6W4B1W
optionC: WWBBA
explanation: RLE stores (count; value) pairs: 6W 4B 1W is a standard representation.

text: Why is lossy compression often acceptable for music and video files?
optionA: Because human senses cannot perceive all the removed detail
optionB: Because music and video do not need to be saved
optionC: Because lossy files always sound exactly the same as originals
optionD: Because music and video are already in binary format
explanation: Lossy compression discards data that is at the edges of human auditory or visual perception; so users rarely notice the difference.

text: What are two main benefits of compressing files for transmission over the internet?
optionA: Faster encryption and improved screen resolution
optionB: Less bandwidth required and faster transmission time
optionC: Improved colour quality and reduced CPU usage
optionD: Better security and larger file capacity
explanation: Smaller compressed files take less bandwidth and transfer more quickly.

text: A file row contains: RRRRGGGGGGRR. How many values does RLE need to describe this row?
explanation: 4R 6G 2R — RLE describes this in 3 count-value pairs.

text: Which statement about Huffman coding is correct?
optionA: Huffman coding is a lossy algorithm used for video only
optionB: Huffman coding assigns shorter codes to more frequently occurring symbols to reduce file size
optionC: Huffman coding works by removing alternate bits from a file
optionD: Huffman coding only compresses images
explanation: Huffman coding uses frequency-based variable-length codes; common characters get shorter codes to minimise total bits used.

text: A JPEG image loses detail compared to the original photograph. What type of compression has been applied?
optionA: Lossless
optionB: Huffman
optionC: Lossless with encryption
optionD: Lossy
explanation: JPEG uses lossy compression; discarding pixel detail that is less noticeable to human vision.

text: Why might a web designer choose to compress images before uploading them to a website?
optionA: To make the images look better on screen
optionB: To reduce the bandwidth required when users load the page
optionC: To add copyright protection to the images
optionD: To convert images from colour to black and white
explanation: Compressed images have smaller file sizes; so they download faster and use less server bandwidth.

text: A 10 MB file is compressed to 2.5 MB using lossless compression. What is the compression ratio?
explanation: 10 MB ÷ 2.5 MB = 4; so the compression ratio is 4:1.

text: Which factor has the BIGGEST impact on how well run-length encoding compresses an image?
optionA: The number of colours used
optionB: The file format of the image
optionC: The length of repeated runs of the same colour
optionD: The resolution of the image
explanation: RLE efficiency depends on how many consecutive identical values appear; more repeats = better compression.

text: After lossy compression is applied to an audio file; which statement is true?
optionA: The file can be fully restored to its original quality using decompression
optionB: Some audio data is permanently lost and cannot be recovered
optionC: The file size stays the same but the audio plays faster
optionD: The file is converted to a lossless format automatically
explanation: Lossy compression permanently discards data; decompression cannot restore what was removed.

text: A graphic designer is archiving original vector designs that must be reopened and edited without quality loss. Which compression type should they use?
optionA: Lossy only
optionB: Either lossy or lossless — it makes no difference
optionC: Lossless
optionD: No compression
explanation: Lossless compression must be used for documents that need to be edited; since all original data is preserved.

text: Why do computers use binary to represent all forms of data?
optionA: Binary is the fastest number system
optionB: Computers are built from transistors that have only two states: on and off
optionC: Binary was chosen because it is easiest for humans to read
optionD: Binary allows negative numbers to be stored more easily
explanation: A transistor can be in one of two states (conducting/not conducting); naturally representing 0 and 1.

text: Which of the following correctly lists the data units from smallest to largest?
optionA: Bit; byte; nibble; KiB; MiB
optionB: Nibble; bit; byte; KiB; GiB
optionC: Bit; nibble; byte; KiB; MiB; GiB
optionD: Byte; bit; KiB; nibble; MiB
explanation: Bit (1) < nibble (4 bits) < byte (8 bits) < KiB (1024 bytes) < MiB < GiB and so on.

text: How many bytes are in 1 kibibyte (KiB)?
explanation: 1 KiB = 2^10 = 1024 bytes (kibibyte uses powers of 2; unlike the decimal kilobyte of 1000 bytes).

text: A file is 5 MiB in size. How many bytes is that?
How many bits make up one nibble?
explanation: A nibble is 4 bits (half a byte).

text: How many bytes make up one mebibyte (MiB)?
A digital photograph has a resolution of 800 × 600 pixels and a colour depth of 24 bits. What is the uncompressed file size in kilobytes? (1 KiB = 1024 bytes)
Convert hexadecimal 2B to denary.
What is the hexadecimal representation of the binary number 1001 0111?
optionD: A7

text: How many bits can be represented by two hexadecimal digits?
explanation: One hex digit = 4 bits; two hex digits = 8 bits (one byte).
